world.wasteland.desc: The bombs are forty years downwind. Water is currency, lead is law, and everything you own was pried out of someone else's wreck.
wasteland.npc.1.desc: Your sister, a scavenger who can hear an undetonated shell through a foot of rubble.
wasteland.npc.1.l1: I found a tin of peaches, still sealed. We eat like kings tonight—or we sell it.
wasteland.npc.1.l2: Don't die for scrap, all right? I already buried one family.
wasteland.npc.2.desc: A one-armed mechanic who talks to engines and trusts no water he did not boil himself.
wasteland.npc.2.l1: The engine's honest. It only lies when you do.
wasteland.npc.2.l2: You drink from my canteen, you drink what I drink. That is the whole treaty.
wasteland.npc.3.desc: A weathered scavenger who has looted every ruin on the map and lied about all of them.
wasteland.npc.3.l1: Rule one: the dead don't mind if you take their boots. The living do.
wasteland.npc.3.l2: A full magazine makes you brave. A full canteen makes you smart.
wasteland.npc.4.desc: The Cistern's quartermaster, who measures water by the thimble and mercy by the gram.
wasteland.npc.4.l1: Three bullets, one liter. I don't haggle, I ration.
wasteland.npc.4.l2: You call it cruelty. I call it the only reason the pumps still turn.
wasteland.npc.5.desc: A caravan driver who hauls salt, fuel, and other people's secrets down the Long Road.
wasteland.npc.5.l1: Passengers talk in their sleep. I charge extra for that.
wasteland.npc.5.l2: The road eats the slow and the honest. Be neither.
wasteland.npc.6.desc: Your mother, a bone-setter with steady hands and a debt she never names.
wasteland.npc.6.l1: Hold still. This will hurt more if you flinch.
wasteland.npc.6.l2: Your father went out for water. I keep the lamp lit anyway.
wasteland.npc.7.desc: A feral kid with a slingshot and a grin, already quicker to kill than most grown men.
wasteland.npc.7.l1: I saw you first. That means your boots are mine, if I want them.
wasteland.npc.7.l2: You were somebody, once. I never was. Guess which one survives.
wasteland.npc.8.desc: A burned-out soldier who bars the door at night and fights like he is still owed something.
wasteland.npc.8.l1: I dug graves for a living before this. Now I just dig.
wasteland.npc.8.l2: You watch the horizon. I watch the door. Nobody sleeps.
wasteland.npc.9.desc: A wandering merchant who can price anything—water, bullets, a name—and teaches the same.
wasteland.npc.9.l1: Everything is for sale. The trick is finding what a man won't sell, and buying that first.
wasteland.npc.9.l2: Never lie about your wares. Lie about your reserves.
wasteland.npc.10.desc: The masked keeper of the last clean well, who decides who drinks and who walks.
wasteland.npc.10.l1: The well doesn't care who you were. It cares what you carry.
wasteland.npc.10.l2: Everyone wants a sip. Almost no one wants to haul the bucket.
wasteland.era.1.desc: The sky caught fire and the cities folded. Whatever survived went underground and counted the quiet.
wasteland.era.2.desc: No engines, no radios, no news. A generation learned to live off rust and rain—if there was rain.
wasteland.era.3.desc: Everything left standing was fought over twice: once for the metal, once for the memory.
wasteland.era.4.desc: The rivers died first, then the wells. Armies marched on the last cistern and called it a nation.
wasteland.era.5.desc: The raiders and the barons signed in blood and diesel: the roads open, the wells stay guarded, no one drinks free.
wasteland.era.6.desc: Weeds push through the glass flats. Nobody trusts it; everybody waters it anyway.
wasteland.fac.1.desc: The water barons. They own the pumps, the rations, and the debt of every throat in the wastes.
wasteland.fac.2.desc: A raider clan born in a burnt-out factory, who take what the caravans cannot defend.
wasteland.fac.3.desc: Armed traders who keep the Long Road open at gunpoint and charge for the privilege.
wasteland.fac.4.desc: Smugglers, bullet-doctors, and brokers. If it cannot be bought, they will find who can sell it.
wasteland.fac.5.desc: Masked guardians of the old wells, half mechanics and half priests, who ration by a law older than any baron.
wasteland.reg.1.desc: The last deep well, ringed by concrete and gun nests; whoever holds the pump holds the wastes.
wasteland.reg.2.desc: A dead city scavenged down to its ribs; steel bones and the occasional booby trap.
wasteland.reg.3.desc: Sand fused to black mirror where the bombs fell; beautiful, and it cooks you by noon.
wasteland.reg.4.desc: A bazaar built on a dead rail yard, where everything has a price and nothing has a receipt.
wasteland.reg.5.desc: The cracked highway where caravans haul salt to trade for water, one ambush at a time.
wasteland.reg.6.desc: A beached sea. Ships stand in the dust, their holds picked clean and their masts still pointing home.
wasteland.reg.7.desc: The ruined interstate that stitches the wastes together—and where most travelers end.
wasteland.lore.1.body: It wasn't one bomb. It was a season of them, low and green, until the dust went up and the sun went dim. Survivors say the worst part wasn't the light—it was how long the quiet lasted after.
wasteland.lore.2.body: For a generation the wastes had no machines and no news. People forgot what a radio was, then remembered a rumor of one, then killed over it.
wasteland.lore.3.body: Every ruin was a fortune and a grave. Men who could weld became kings; men who could read became suspects.
wasteland.lore.4.body: The barons and the raiders signed in blood and diesel. The roads opened. So did the tolls.
wasteland.lore.5.body: In the wastes, a man who says nothing is for sale is either a saint or a liar. Most liars are better shots.
wasteland.lore.6.body: The dead don't mind if you take their boots. Only the living keep a ledger of what's owed.
wasteland.lore.7.body: They will tell you kindness is a luxury. Then the drought comes, and the one man who shared his canteen is the one nobody shoots.
wasteland.lore.8: The Well Belongs to the Thirsty
wasteland.lore.8.body: Some say the well belongs to the strong, some to the first. The thirsty say it belongs to whoever is drinking.
wasteland.lore.9.body: Everyone who walks the Long Road learns the same lesson: a homeland, out here, is just a place you haven't had to leave yet.
wasteland.lore.10.body: At sixty you count two things—bullets and birthdays—and you stop being surprised which runs out first.
wasteland.lore.11.body: Weeds in the glass flats. Something in the soil remembered how. Nobody says the word 'hope' aloud; they just water it.
wasteland.lore.12.body: The best scavengers don't read maps. They read silence—where the birds went, where the dogs won't go, where the sand was turned yesterday.
wasteland.lore.13.body: At thirty every survivor keeps two ledgers: what they have taken, and what was taken from them. The second is always longer.
wasteland.lore.14.body: A good bullet-doctor can save you for a clip and a promise. The promise is the expensive part.
wasteland.lore.15: The One Who Fed the Dogs
wasteland.lore.15.body: An old woman fed the wild dogs at the edge of the Cistern. When the raiders came, the dogs knew her name.
wasteland.lore.16.body: They say there is a well no baron has found, and whoever drinks from it walks into the green places. The Well-Keepers say nothing, which is answer enough.
wasteland.fate.1.desc: You will learn every ruin by its smell and die rich in everything except time.
wasteland.fate.2.desc: You will own a well and the throats around it, and never once drink without checking the water first.
wasteland.fate.3.desc: You will stitch a hundred strangers and be buried by the one who remembered your name.
wasteland.fate.4.desc: You will take what you need and need more every year, until taking is all you know.
wasteland.fate.5.desc: You will outlive your enemies and your friends, and keep the lights on out of sheer stubbornness.
wasteland.fate.6.desc: You will stand at the last clean water and decide, once, who drinks and who keeps walking.
wasteland.we.1.body: One year the rains simply don't come. The old men call it a dry spell; the old women start digging deeper.
wasteland.we.2.body: Two barons claim the same pump. By winter the Cistern is one baron richer and one village lighter.
wasteland.we.3.body: The last factory coughs out its final casing. For a season, a bullet is worth more than the man it is aimed at.
wasteland.we.4.body: The raiders sign. The caravans pay. The hills go quiet, and everyone spends the quiet sharpening something.
wasteland.we.5.body: A rad-wind drags glass dust off the flats. Whole caravans come in with their voices sanded away.
wasteland.we.6.body: Grass, real grass, at the edge of the Bonefield. The Wells ring a bell nobody has heard in forty years.
wasteland.ev.stranger.1: A Stranger at the Line — Cistern
wasteland.ev.stranger.1.text: At the Cistern's ration line a scavenger with heat-scarred hands offers you half his canteen for word carried back to Sable.
wasteland.ev.stranger.1.listen.note: It was her brother's last words, and half a canteen of water he could not spare to give.
wasteland.ev.stranger.1.turn.note: You walked the Salt Line without water and kept his name unspoken until dark.
wasteland.ev.stranger.2: A Man on Foot — Long Road
wasteland.ev.stranger.2.text: A man with one boot waves you down on the Long Road, saying the Rustborn burned his caravan last night and he has walked since.
wasteland.ev.stranger.2.listen.note: He talked till dawn and never once asked what was in your pack. Almost never.
wasteland.ev.stranger.2.turn.note: He came at your pack with a length of pipe; you put him in the dust and limped on.
wasteland.ev.stranger.3.text: A masked novice of the Well-Keepers corners you in Rustmarket and asks to buy your silence about the face beneath her mask.
wasteland.ev.stranger.3.listen.note: She traded a rumor of a clean spring under the Glass Flats, and you kept her face.
wasteland.ev.stranger.3.turn.note: She was gone before you finished the word, and the rumor of the spring with her.
wasteland.ev.stranger.4: The Woman at the Wheel — Dry Harbor
wasteland.ev.stranger.4.text: At Dry Harbor a woman tending a dead ship's wheel says she crewed the last convoy out of the Cistern, and will read your fortune for a mouthful of water.
wasteland.ev.stranger.4.listen.note: She named your mother and the year your father left. You did not sleep well after that.
wasteland.ev.stranger.4.turn.note: She shrugged and turned the wheel toward a sea that is no longer there.
wasteland.ev.theft.1.text: In the crush of Rustmarket a child slips your pouch of rounds from your belt, and the crowd closes behind him.
wasteland.ev.theft.1.chase.note: You caught him by the tracks; he was eight, and crying for his sister's medicine.
wasteland.ev.theft.1.yield.note: Six rounds gone. You counted the rest that night like losses.
wasteland.ev.theft.2.text: You wake at the waystation to a loose cap and a canteen lighter by half, and a shape moving off along the rail bed.
wasteland.ev.theft.2.chase.note: A Fixer's runner, hired to top off his master's tab. You took back the canteen and a name.
wasteland.ev.theft.2.yield.note: Half your water gone. You learned to sleep with the strap around your wrist.
wasteland.ev.theft.3.text: You turn your back on the dig for one hour, and someone has stripped the copper you spent three days cutting free.
wasteland.ev.theft.3.chase.note: The trail ran to a Rustborn camp. You took back the copper and left with the fear still on you.
wasteland.ev.theft.3.yield.note: Three days of scraping, gone. The wire cost more to cut than the copper was worth.
wasteland.ev.theft.4.text: On the Salt Line you notice your hired guard has been skimming salt from every sack, and the Cistern weighs its toll to the grain.
wasteland.ev.theft.4.chase.note: He paid it back in salt and would not meet your eye again. Mother Price noticed both.
wasteland.ev.theft.4.yield.note: You paid the toll short and ate the difference. He rode easier than you did.
wasteland.ev.illness.1.text: You cross the Glass Flats too near noon, and by night your gums ache and your skin burns where the wind touched it.
wasteland.ev.illness.1.nurse: Walk it off at the dig
wasteland.ev.illness.1.nurse.note: You worked the wreck until you dropped, and the dose in your bones has not left.
wasteland.ev.illness.1.avoid.note: You lost two days of work and slept with a dosimeter clicking beside your head.
wasteland.ev.illness.2.text: The ration line at the Cistern is handing out something green and quick, and by evening your stomach is in knots.
wasteland.ev.illness.2.nurse.note: You hauled buckets until you saw two wells, and the shakes stayed a week.
wasteland.ev.illness.2.avoid.note: You burned half your fuel sterilizing water and missed the shift, but kept your name off the fever list.
wasteland.ev.illness.3.text: The cut from the Rustmarket brawl is turning black at the edges, and the bullet-doctor wants a full canteen just to look at it.
wasteland.ev.illness.3.nurse.note: Your mother's hands were steady and her eyes were not. The iodine hurt worse than the blade.
wasteland.ev.illness.3.avoid.note: The leg held, thin and angry, and you limp the morning after every rain.
wasteland.ev.illness.4: Cough in the Camp — Salt Line
wasteland.ev.illness.4.text: The caravan's youngest driver has a cough that rattles, and the rule of the road is simple: the sick walk behind.
wasteland.ev.illness.4.nurse: Share your water and ride close
wasteland.ev.illness.4.nurse.note: You gave him your tin and heard him cough all night. Half the crew caught it, and none of them blamed you aloud.
wasteland.ev.illness.4.avoid.note: He fell behind on the third day and was not there on the fourth. The caravan did not slow.
wasteland.ev.windfall.1.text: A dead prospector's map lands in your hands, marking a salt pan worth more than a season of scavving.
wasteland.ev.windfall.1.invest.note: You split the haul three ways and bought better boots for every one of them.
wasteland.ev.windfall.1.save: Sell the map and stay light
wasteland.ev.windfall.1.save.note: The buyer got rich. You got enough to matter, and no one at your back to watch.
wasteland.ev.windfall.2.text: A Fixer swears a sealed crate of pre-Burn batteries lies under the rail yard, and only needs a buyer to pay for the dig.
wasteland.ev.windfall.2.invest.note: The crate was half water-logged, and the half that was not made you a name in Rustmarket.
wasteland.ev.windfall.2.save: Keep your coin and your hands clean
wasteland.ev.windfall.2.save.note: They dug without you. The crate was empty, and you heard about it for a month.
wasteland.ev.windfall.3.text: An old well-keeper dies and leaves you the row she owed the Conclave, and a key that opens a cistern door.
wasteland.ev.windfall.3.invest: Pay the debt and claim the key
wasteland.ev.windfall.3.invest.note: Mother Price watched you square the ledger. Something in her accounting softened, barely.
wasteland.ev.windfall.3.save: Sell the key, let the debt lie
wasteland.ev.windfall.3.save.note: The Conclave forgave what it could not collect. The key opened a room someone had emptied first.
wasteland.ev.windfall.4.text: Your caravan's ram survives a raid untouched, and the crew votes to sell it at the Cistern for water.
wasteland.ev.windfall.4.invest: Ride it to the Cistern and trade high
wasteland.ev.windfall.4.invest.note: The ram fetched a drum of fuel and the crew's first hot meal in weeks.
wasteland.ev.windfall.4.save: Keep the ram for the herd
wasteland.ev.windfall.4.save.note: The ram sired a line that outlived three of the men who voted with you.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.1.text: Your partner sold the salvage from the Dry Harbor cache twice over: once to the Trader, once to a Rustborn quartermaster.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.1.confront.note: He went white in front of the whole market. The partnership died louder than it ever lived.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.1.plan: Say nothing and keep the ledger
wasteland.ev.betrayal.1.plan.note: You let him think it was forgotten, and moved your cut somewhere only you could reach.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.2.text: You learn the Fixer you paid to guard your ration tab has been drawing from it all month, in your name.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.2.confront.note: He talked his way clear and you lost the tab anyway. The quartermaster said nothing, which cost more.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.2.plan.note: When the Conclave audited, your name was clean and his was the only one dirty.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.3.text: A scavenger you trained has been copying your route maps and selling the marks to the Rustborn, and one of your caches is already gone.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.3.confront.note: He swung first. You kept the maps and the limp, and told no one where he went.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.3.plan.note: The Rustborn raided an empty ruin and blamed him. You never had to raise your voice.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.4.text: A caravan crew reaches the Cistern saying it was you who cut the tow rope and left their truck for the raiders.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.4.confront.note: The crew did not believe you, but the driver did, and that was one more ally than yesterday.
wasteland.ev.betrayal.4.plan.note: A Fixer with your scar and your drawl. You kept his face in your pocket until you needed it.
wasteland.ev.festival.1.text: The Cistern cracks one well open for a single night, and the whole wastes drinks together, or drinks near enough.
wasteland.ev.festival.1.join: Stand in the line and drink
wasteland.ev.festival.1.join.note: Strangers traded rumors with you over the cups, and one of them kept your face for later.
wasteland.ev.festival.1.work: Guard the stores while they celebrate
wasteland.ev.festival.1.work.note: You were paid double to watch the drunk and the doors, and heard the singing from outside.
wasteland.ev.festival.2.text: Rustmarket lights its rail fires and trades stories and scrap, and every Fixer in the wastes comes out to be seen.
wasteland.ev.festival.2.join.note: You traded three lies for a true map, and woke with a lighter pocket and a lighter heart.
wasteland.ev.festival.2.work.note: Your scrap cleared a full season's price while the fires burned, and you never once left the table.
wasteland.ev.festival.3.text: The Caravan Companies mark the Truce with a meal on the Long Road, and raider and trader eat at the same fire for one night.
wasteland.ev.festival.3.join.note: You ate beside a Rustborn who had burned a camp you knew, and neither of you said a word about it.
wasteland.ev.festival.3.work.note: The Truce held because someone stayed sober. That someone was you, and the Companies noted it.
wasteland.ev.festival.4.text: Weeds have pushed through the black glass, and the Well-Keepers hold a quiet gathering to water them and say nothing aloud.
wasteland.ev.festival.4.join: Bring water and stand with them
wasteland.ev.festival.4.join.note: The Keeper nodded once. Nobody spoke the word hope, but the dirt was wet and everyone saw.
wasteland.ev.festival.4.work.note: You cleared good coin off a crowd too busy hoping to haggle, and felt the worse for it by morning.
wasteland.ev.rumor.1.text: A drunk at Rustmarket swears he drank from a well with no rust and no baron, somewhere past the Glass Flats.
wasteland.ev.rumor.1.trace.note: The story unraveled into a con, but the road he described was real and worth walking.
wasteland.ev.rumor.1.ignore: Let the drunk keep his well
wasteland.ev.rumor.1.ignore.note: You told yourself it was nothing, and kept walking toward the flats anyway.
wasteland.ev.rumor.2.text: Word at the Cistern says your father was seen alive on the Salt Line, wearing another man's name.
wasteland.ev.rumor.2.trace.note: Two drivers remembered the face. Neither remembered the name he gave, and that was answer enough.
wasteland.ev.rumor.2.ignore.note: The lamp stayed lit that night, same as always, and you did not look at it.
wasteland.ev.rumor.3.text: A scout claims the Rustborn are massing behind the dunes, and the caravans are arguing whether to believe him.
wasteland.ev.rumor.3.trace: Ride out and see for yourself
wasteland.ev.rumor.3.trace.note: You found the tracks and said nothing to the convoy. They doubled the watch without knowing why.
wasteland.ev.rumor.3.ignore.note: The Truce held. The scout was never seen again, and you wondered for a long time which fact mattered.
wasteland.ev.rumor.4.text: A story moves through Dry Harbor of a spring under a beached ship, clean enough to drink and deep enough to sell.
wasteland.ev.rumor.4.trace.note: You found a foot of seawater and rust, and a rumor now nailed down to a real place.
wasteland.ev.rumor.4.ignore.note: Three crews dug that hull. None came back rich, and one came back short a man.
wasteland.ev.journey.1: The Long Road West — Salt Line
wasteland.ev.journey.1.text: A caravan bound for the far cisterns is short a guard and will pay in water for the miles.
wasteland.ev.journey.1.go.note: You saw three towns you had only heard named, and one of them could use a hand like yours.
wasteland.ev.journey.1.stay.note: The caravan rolled out at dawn. You worked the same salvage pile and slept in the same dust.
wasteland.ev.journey.2.text: Rust knows a ruin under the Bonefield that no one has stripped, and he will not go alone.
wasteland.ev.journey.2.go.note: The ruin was good, the old man's knee was not, and you carried him out with the loot.
wasteland.ev.journey.2.stay: Let the old man keep his story
wasteland.ev.journey.2.stay.note: Rust came back with a limp and a grin and refused to say what he found.
wasteland.ev.journey.3.text: Dust offers you a place on a run to the Dry Harbor, where a ship still stands with its holds sealed.
wasteland.ev.journey.3.go.note: The holds were mostly sand, but the chart table held a map of the Long Road from before the Burn.
wasteland.ev.journey.3.stay: Let the seas keep their dead
wasteland.ev.journey.3.stay.note: Dust's crew came back with rope and bone and no cargo worth the diesel.
wasteland.ev.journey.4.text: The Well-Keeper says the green is spreading past the flats, and means to walk out and see how far the water has come.
wasteland.ev.journey.4.go.note: Two days out you stood in real grass, and the masked old man took off his mask and wept.
wasteland.ev.journey.4.stay.note: The Keeper returned alone at dusk and said only that the ground was softer than before.
wasteland.ev.duel.1.text: In Rustmarket a Fixer sets cans on a girder at fifty paces and bets water that you cannot clear them.
wasteland.ev.duel.1.fight.note: You cleared five of six, and the one you missed cost you the pot and taught you the wind.
wasteland.ev.duel.1.decline.note: He kept the water and the story, and the market drank to your name being yellow.
wasteland.ev.duel.2.text: A caravan hand takes the cut of your salt as an insult and draws a knife by the cook fire, saying it should be settled properly.
wasteland.ev.duel.2.fight.note: You drew first blood and bought his silence with it; he rode beside you the rest of the way.
wasteland.ev.duel.2.decline.note: He spat and called you soft. You kept both hands and both eyes, and watched your back for a week.
wasteland.ev.duel.3.text: The Boy, feral and quick, says your claim is his by right of sight and offers to fight for the salvage.
wasteland.ev.duel.3.fight.note: He was faster than anything that size had a right to be. You won, and still he grinned.
wasteland.ev.duel.3.decline.note: You gave him half, and by spring he was bringing you things he had found on his own.
wasteland.ev.duel.4.text: Ash, drunk and owed something by the world, calls you out in the Cistern yard and will not be talked down.
wasteland.ev.duel.4.fight.note: He fought like a man twice owed. You put him in the dust, and he thanked you before he passed out.
wasteland.ev.duel.4.decline.note: He shouted your name at the concrete until the Well-Keepers came. You were already gone.
wasteland.ev.harvest.1.text: A row of root vegetables comes up in the cracked glass, the first real food anyone has grown there in forty years.
wasteland.ev.harvest.1.share: Share the row with the camp
wasteland.ev.harvest.1.share.note: Everyone ate something green that night, and the Well-Keepers rang a bell not heard since before the Burn.
wasteland.ev.harvest.1.hoard: Pull it all and bury it in your stash
wasteland.ev.harvest.1.hoard.note: You ate well and told no one. The row did not come up again the next year.
wasteland.ev.harvest.2.text: A rad-wind finally breaks into rain over the Cistern, and the catch barrels fill faster than anyone can haul them in.
wasteland.ev.harvest.2.share: Give the overflow to the line
wasteland.ev.harvest.2.share.note: The crowd drank and remembered who held the barrel. The Conclave remembered too, less kindly.
wasteland.ev.harvest.2.hoard.note: You came out of the storm with two barrels no ledger would ever show.
wasteland.ev.harvest.3.text: You clear a collapsed store under the Bonefield and find sealed rations enough to feed a crew for a month.
wasteland.ev.harvest.3.share: Carry it back to the camp
wasteland.ev.harvest.3.share.note: Half the camp ate your beans, and half of them resented you by the time the tins ran out.
wasteland.ev.harvest.3.hoard: Hide it where only you know
wasteland.ev.harvest.3.hoard.note: You never had to ask anyone for food again, and never trusted a soul enough to say so.
wasteland.ev.harvest.4.text: Your caravan's salt haul comes in heavy, and the Cistern will pay a premium for every sack above the contract.
wasteland.ev.harvest.4.share: Split the surplus with the crew
wasteland.ev.harvest.4.share.note: The drivers drank your share with you, and every one of them marked the favor down.
wasteland.ev.harvest.4.hoard.note: The money was real. So was the driver who stopped meeting your eye on the road.
wasteland.ev.law.1.text: The Conclave nails a new notice to the Cistern gate: no water without a ration tab, and the Keepers are ordered to shoot the second bucket.
wasteland.ev.law.1.obey.note: You queue with the others and drink by the thimble. Sable's canteen hangs empty on her belt, and neither of you mentions it.
wasteland.ev.law.1.defy.note: You come back at midnight with a rope and a bottle. The well never tells, but the rope burns your palms for a week.
wasteland.ev.law.2.text: The Fixers now charge a toll on every cart that crosses the dead rail yard, and they want it paid in ammunition.
wasteland.ev.law.2.obey.note: You hand over a clip and keep your salvage. The Fixers start waving you through by name, which is worse than a toll.
wasteland.ev.law.2.defy.note: You drag your cart through the Bonefield instead. The sandcut takes a boot and half a day, and the Fixers remember your face.
wasteland.ev.law.3.text: The Well-Keeper's law is older than any baron: no one drinks who has not hauled. A stranger offers you his bucket and asks you to cover for him.
wasteland.ev.law.3.obey.note: You rope up and pull till your shoulders burn. The Keeper nods once and fills your canteen, and the stranger walks away dry.
wasteland.ev.law.3.defy.note: You lie for him and he drinks. The Keeper says nothing, and never fills your canteen again.
wasteland.ev.law.4.text: Mother Price opens a debt line at the Cistern: take water now, work it off at the pumps. She slides the ration ledger across the table.
wasteland.ev.law.4.obey.note: You sign and drink deep. The ledger leans over your shoulder every morning, and Mother Price calls you by your number now.
wasteland.ev.law.4.defy.note: You leave with a dry throat and a free name. Pride is a poor canteen, but it is yours, and it is not written down.
wasteland.ev.first_love.1.text: You have queued at the Cistern pump for three hours when the girl ahead of you turns, shares a sip from her tin, and the whole line disappears.
wasteland.ev.first_love.1.woo.note: You haul her water the whole way and forget to fill your own. She leaves you half a liter, and the taste of it lasts a month.
wasteland.ev.first_love.1.friend.note: You trade names at the gate and nothing more. For a season the pump is the best part of your morning, and you never say why.
wasteland.ev.first_love.2.text: At Rustmarket a girl sells you a dented canteen, then laughs and gives it free when she watches you count your caps twice.
wasteland.ev.first_love.2.woo: Ask her to the Salt Line at dusk
wasteland.ev.first_love.2.woo.note: She says the road eats the slow, then takes your hand anyway. You walk the cracked highway until the moon is high, and neither of you sells anything.
wasteland.ev.first_love.2.friend.note: You keep buying canteens you do not need. She never notices, and you never tell her, and the shelf at home fills with dents.
wasteland.ev.first_love.3.text: In the beached harbor a scavenger your age is stripping wire from a wreck, and teaches you the trick for nothing but company.
wasteland.ev.first_love.3.woo.note: You share a fire in a dead ship's hold and talk till the stars come out over the masts. You wake first, and watch them sleep, and say nothing.
wasteland.ev.first_love.3.friend.note: You pocket the trick and go at dusk with your copper and your quiet. You think about that hold for years, and never find the ship again.
wasteland.ev.first_love.4.text: A caravan camps at the edge of your settlement for one night, and a driver's daughter asks you to watch the fire with her.
wasteland.ev.first_love.4.woo: Walk out with her at dawn
wasteland.ev.first_love.4.woo.note: You walk beside the wagon until the road bends. She kisses you once and the caravan takes her anyway, and you stand in the dust a long time.
wasteland.ev.first_love.4.friend.note: You swap stories till dawn and never learn her name. The caravan leaves, and so does the chance, and you remember the fire longer than the face.
wasteland.ev.grief.1.text: Rust went into the Bonefield alone for one last haul and came back on a stretcher. He dies at your fire before the sun clears the ribs.
wasteland.ev.grief.1.mourn.note: You stay with the body till the heat bakes it. You do not eat for two days, and you never forget the way his one good hand was still reaching.
wasteland.ev.grief.1.carry: Bury him and take his boots
wasteland.ev.grief.1.carry.note: You lace on his boots and dig him under the rusted girder. Every step after is partly his, and they fit better than yours ever did.
wasteland.ev.grief.2.text: Word comes down the Long Road: Ash walked into a rad pocket and did not walk out. They found his rifle, not him.
wasteland.ev.grief.2.mourn.note: You walk three days to the spot and stand in the clicking silence. You leave his rifle where it lay, and the geiger counts for both of you.
wasteland.ev.grief.2.carry.note: You pour a cap of fuel on the fire and say nothing. You keep his watch, and it keeps ticking, and you stop winding it a year later.
wasteland.ev.grief.3.text: The cough that went through the camp takes the youngest boy in the next lean-to. His mother asks you to carry the body out past the well.
wasteland.ev.grief.3.mourn.note: You wrap him in a fuel tarp and carry him past the pump. The weight stays in your arms for weeks, and you flinch when children run at you.
wasteland.ev.grief.3.carry.note: You give the gravediggers your last caps and go back to work. The shovel rings in your ears all day, and you do not look up the street.
wasteland.ev.grief.4.text: A trader you shared water with for years is found dead beside his cart on the Salt Line, shot for his cargo.
wasteland.ev.grief.4.mourn.note: You dig in the cracked asphalt and mark it with his axle. You cannot remember his real name, only the way he always capped a canteen before passing it.
wasteland.ev.grief.4.carry.note: You harness his mule and finish his route. The buyers never ask, and you never tell them, and you drink from his canteen at every stop.
wasteland.ev.craft.1.text: Cog offers to teach you the one-armed trick of rebuilding a pump — if you give him your hands and half your water for a month.
wasteland.ev.craft.1.take.note: You spend a month wrist-deep in diesel and cut knuckles. When the pump turns the first time, Cog grins and calls you a mechanic, and you believe him.
wasteland.ev.craft.1.refuse.note: You walk away with a full canteen and no trade. The pump breaks again next spring, and you pay another man with the water you saved.
wasteland.ev.craft.2.text: A Fixer shows you how to pull a bullet and pack a wound with iodine and clean rag, asking only that you never work his street.
wasteland.ev.craft.2.take.note: You learn to close a chest wound on a table of scrap. Your hands stop shaking after the third one, and you stop counting the ones who do not make it.
wasteland.ev.craft.2.refuse.note: You leave the needle on his table and keep the iodine. You keep paying him to use it, every time, for years.
wasteland.ev.craft.3.text: An old armorer in the Gunworks offers to teach you to reload casings, saying ammunition is the only honest currency left in the wastes.
wasteland.ev.craft.3.take.note: You learn to measure powder by eye and seat a primer by feel. Your clip lasts twice as long, and men ride a day out of their way for your loads.
wasteland.ev.craft.3.refuse.note: You leave the powder untouched. Your rifle stays hungry through the dry season, and you count every round like a coin.
wasteland.ev.craft.4.text: A scavenger offers to teach you to read a ruin: where the floor holds, where the gas sleeps, where the good metal is buried.
wasteland.ev.craft.4.take.note: You learn to hear a rotten floor before it drops you. You come out of the Bonefield more often than you go in, and that is the whole trade.
wasteland.ev.craft.4.refuse.note: You keep scavenging on nerve alone. It works, right up until the day a stair gives out under your boot, and then it does not.
wasteland.ev.secret.1.text: You find the Well-Keeper unmasked beside the well, and recognize the baron's son the Conclave hanged years ago — alive, and hoarding clean water.
wasteland.ev.secret.1.open.note: You sell the name for a canteen of clean water. The well is quieter after, and so are you, and you drink fast so you do not have to taste it.
wasteland.ev.secret.1.leave.note: You say nothing and take your ration. Every time he fills your canteen you look at the masked face and away, and the water never tastes right again.
wasteland.ev.secret.2.text: You find a dead scavenger in the Bonefield with a map to a buried cache sewn into his coat, stamped with the Cistern's own sigil.
wasteland.ev.secret.2.open.note: You trade it at Rustmarket for a rifle and a season of fuel. Someone else digs there, and does not come back, and you keep the rifle loaded.
wasteland.ev.secret.2.leave.note: You fold the coat back over his chest and fill the grave in. You dream about the cache for a year, and never once go looking.
wasteland.ev.secret.3.text: You catch the Boy in the middle of the night with a stolen canister of fuel — and a dog bite laid open down his forearm.
wasteland.ev.secret.3.open.note: You turn him in for the reward. The camp hangs a boy for a drum of fuel and calls it order, and the grins stop when you walk past.
wasteland.ev.secret.3.leave.note: You stitch his arm with fishing line and split your fuel. He is gone before first light, and he never robs you again, and he never thanks you either.
wasteland.ev.secret.4.text: You learn Ash deserted in the Water Wars and left his squad to die; the graves he is so proud of digging were his own men's.
wasteland.ev.secret.4.open.note: You give the veterans the truth and a place to point it. They walk him out past the wire, and his cot is empty by morning, and you sleep fine.
wasteland.ev.secret.4.leave.note: You keep his secret and share his fire. He drinks less now and watches the door harder, and you both know what the other is not saying.
wasteland.ev.drought.1.text: The Cistern drops a meter overnight. Mother Price cuts every ration by half, and the queue turns ugly by noon.
wasteland.ev.drought.1.ration.note: You drink a cup a day and learn to count by the swallow. It is never enough, and after a while you stop complaining, which frightens you more.
wasteland.ev.drought.1.take.note: You fill every canteen while the line watches. You drink tonight and sleep with your hand on the gun, and the well gets lower anyway.
wasteland.ev.drought.2.text: The caravan hauls salt toward the Cistern to trade for water, and the midway well has gone dry under the tarps.
wasteland.ev.drought.2.ration.note: You dole the last water out by the capful. The horses go first, and by the third day one man does not get up, and you keep the tally straight.
wasteland.ev.drought.2.take: Take your share and hide it
wasteland.ev.drought.2.take.note: You drink behind the wagon and re-cap the drum. Nobody asks, and you hear them licking their lips all night, and you never tell them.
wasteland.ev.drought.3.text: Water hits a clip a liter in Rustmarket. A Fixer offers you a full drum he 'found' — if you do not ask where from.
wasteland.ev.drought.3.ration.note: You count out your caps for one liter and carry it home like a newborn. It lasts four days, and you learn which four days to give it to.
wasteland.ev.drought.3.take.note: You buy the whole drum and drink properly for the first time in weeks. The man it was stolen from is still walking the Salt Line, and you try not to picture him.
wasteland.ev.drought.4.text: You find a scavenger's still dripping clean water out of the glass flats, hidden under a scorched solar panel. He has been drinking alone out here for months.
wasteland.ev.drought.4.ration.note: You trade him fuel and leave the still in his hands. He shows you the path in for next time, and a map is worth more than a drum.
wasteland.ev.drought.4.take.note: You pull the tubing and cart the still home. It makes water every day, and it makes a scar somewhere you cannot point to, and you drink anyway.
wasteland.ev.gift.1: Gift — The Canteen on the Step
wasteland.ev.gift.1.text: Someone leaves a sealed canteen of clean water on your step in the night, with no mark and no name.
wasteland.ev.gift.1.accept.note: The water is cold and clean and tastes of nothing you own. Out here, kindness is only a debt wearing a friendly face, and you drink it dry.
wasteland.ev.gift.1.suspect.note: You tip it on the sand in case it is poisoned. It was the cleanest water you saw that month, and you think about it every dry night after.
wasteland.ev.gift.2.text: Sable comes back from a haul with a tin of peaches and sets it in front of you, unopened, saying nothing.
wasteland.ev.gift.2.accept.note: You eat half and slide her the rest. She calls you a fool and eats it anyway, grinning with juice on her chin, and for one evening the war is far away.
wasteland.ev.gift.2.suspect.note: You ask what she traded for it. She goes quiet, and you learn it cost her a week of rations, and you cannot enjoy a single peach.
wasteland.ev.gift.3.text: A Fixer leaves a working pistol on your table, wrapped clean in a bullet-doctor's cloth, with no note.
wasteland.ev.gift.3.accept.note: The pistol fires true. Six months later the Fixer comes to collect, and the price is a favor you cannot refuse and will never finish paying.
wasteland.ev.gift.3.suspect.note: You set it in the dust for whoever wants it. It is gone by morning, and so is the bite of the favor, and you keep your old rusted piece.
wasteland.ev.gift.4.text: A caravan leaves a crate of fuel at your door with a note: 'For the one who dug our driver out of the sand last spring.'
wasteland.ev.gift.4.accept.note: You burn their fuel all winter and think of the driver. Kindness, out here, is fuel that comes back to the man who spent it.
wasteland.ev.gift.4.suspect.note: You pry the crate open looking for a trap and find only diesel. There was no trick, and you stand there feeling smaller than the crate.
wasteland.ev.war.1.text: The Rustborn come off the hills at dusk on stripped bikes. The camp has one rifle, no plan, and a gate that does not close.
wasteland.ev.war.1.serve.note: You take the rifle and hold the gate till the engines fade. You are bleeding from the shoulder, and nobody in the camp is dead, and you cannot stop shaking.
wasteland.ev.war.1.hide.note: You put the young ones in the storm cellar and lie on top of the hatch. The raid passes right over you, and you hear every boot, every scream, every shot.
wasteland.ev.war.2.text: Two barons fight over the Cistern pump, and the Conclave conscripts every hand that can hold a rifle up onto the parapet.
wasteland.ev.war.2.serve.note: You stand watch through the shelling and learn what a pump is worth in blood. The Conclave gives you a water tab for it, and you spend the tab, not the memory.
wasteland.ev.war.2.hide.note: You leave through the drainage ditch with a family you never met. You keep your hands clean and your name off the wall, and you never go back to look.
wasteland.ev.war.3.text: A caravan comes under fire on the Long Road, wagons strung out, drivers pinned behind sacks of salt.
wasteland.ev.war.3.serve.note: You lay down fire until the raiders pull back. The Caravan Companies pay you a rifle and a promise, and the promise is the part they intend to keep.
wasteland.ev.war.3.hide.note: You keep your engine running and do not stop. In the mirror the wagons burn, and you sell the sight to yourself as sleep, night after night.
wasteland.ev.war.4.text: The fighting is over. Your settlement is ash, the well is fouled, and the survivors sit in the dust waiting for someone to say what happens now.
wasteland.ev.war.4.serve.note: You walk them down the Long Road to the next water. You count every head at dawn, and you never stop counting, and you are the last to drink.
wasteland.ev.war.4.hide.note: You take your share and leave before first light. They do not blame you, which is worse than blame, and the quiet of the road is the loudest thing you know.
wasteland.ev.famine.1.text: The grain the camp stored through the wet season has gone to weevils and damp. The quartermaster says there is food for ten days, not forty.
wasteland.ev.famine.1.share.note: You split everything by the head. It runs out sooner, and no one in the camp ever watches another person eat, and that is worth something you cannot put in a ledger.
wasteland.ev.famine.1.close.note: You dole out half rations and keep the rest behind the wall. The camp eats, and the camp counts every grain you carry, and you hear them counting.
wasteland.ev.famine.2.text: The family in the next lean-to has not lit a cookfire in three days. Their youngest stares at your pot with the flat patience of the very hungry.
wasteland.ev.famine.2.share.note: You give them half of nothing much. By spring the mother will not let anyone harm you, and the boy still stares, but at your hands, not your pot.
wasteland.ev.famine.2.close.note: You eat with your back to their fire. The boy stops staring, which is somehow worse, and you chew slower than you need to.
wasteland.ev.famine.3.text: The Trader's only food left is a sack of seeds meant for planting. Men are already offering him bullets for it.
wasteland.ev.famine.3.share.note: You pay his price and plant the seeds in poisoned ground. Half come up; the half that come up carry you both through, and he remembers the color of your caps.
wasteland.ev.famine.3.close.note: You buy the seeds and eat them that night. The Trader never sells to you again, and there is nothing left to plant, and you are full and hollow at once.
wasteland.ev.famine.4.text: No rain for a season and the shallow wells are dust. A Well-Keeper opens the old well to whoever can survive the line.
wasteland.ev.famine.4.share: Pour a cup for the weak
wasteland.ev.famine.4.share.note: You give your cup to a woman with a baby and step back into line. She remembers it, and so does the Well-Keeper, and your name travels the flats.
wasteland.ev.famine.4.close.note: You drink till your belly hurts and carry the rest home. You sleep with the taste of clean water and a scared heart, and you avoid the woman's eyes.
wasteland.ev.tradition.1.text: The Well-Keepers hold their old rite at the last clean well: no one speaks while the bucket goes down. A young Keeper asks you to haul.
wasteland.ev.tradition.1.keep.note: You haul without a word while the crowd holds its breath. At the end the Keeper fills your canteen first, and the silence tastes older than the water.
wasteland.ev.tradition.1.break.note: You ask, out loud, why the silence matters. The crowd flinches like you spat, and the Keeper fills your canteen last, and never speaks to you again.
wasteland.ev.tradition.2.text: Rust always said you do not take the boots of a man you did not bury. Tonight the camp strips a stranger's body for gear.
wasteland.ev.tradition.2.keep.note: You walk past the corpse with your hands empty. Rust would be proud; nobody rewards you; and you go to bed colder than the night before.
wasteland.ev.tradition.2.break.note: You pull the boots off and wear them home. They fit, and they make you fast, and you can still feel the man in them every time you lace up.
wasteland.ev.tradition.3.text: The Caravan Companies swear an old oath at the start of every run: no one drinks first, no one eats alone, no one is left on the road.
wasteland.ev.tradition.3.keep.note: You swear to the road and the trucks, and the drivers treat you as one of their own. It is a small kingdom made of diesel and habit, and it holds.
wasteland.ev.tradition.3.break.note: You will not swear to words you do not mean. They let you ride anyway, and watch you at every fire, and no one ever eats alone except you.
wasteland.ev.tradition.4: Tradition — The Ledger of the Dead
wasteland.ev.tradition.4.text: On the last day of the Burn, the Cistern reads its ledger aloud: every name that died still owed water. Mother Price asks whether she should keep reading.
wasteland.ev.tradition.4.keep.note: You stand while the quartermaster reads for hours. The dead cost you a day of water and a pair of boots worn thin, and you would spend it again.
wasteland.ev.tradition.4.break.note: You tell her to stop and count the living instead. The crowd goes home faster and quieter, and no one thanks you, and the names are still in the book.
wasteland.ev.legacy.1.text: Sable pries a dead scavenger's logbook out of a girder pocket. Every page is filled with tallies, but the last page is blank. She hands you the pencil stub without a word.
wasteland.ev.legacy.1.write.note: You added your name under forty years of strangers. Sable watched you do it and stopped asking who you were.
wasteland.ev.legacy.1.silent.note: You closed the book and slid it back under the steel. Somewhere down the Bonefield, a page curled in the wind and took your turn with it.
wasteland.ev.legacy.2.text: Vera's hands shake too hard to thread a needle. She starts dictating her bone-setting remedies across the fire and wants them written down before she loses the words.
wasteland.ev.legacy.2.write.note: You filled three pages of butcher paper with her voice. She fell asleep before the last one, and you already knew which of you the fever would need.
wasteland.ev.legacy.2.silent.note: She stopped mid-remedy and stared into the coals. Everything she knew went unsaid after that, and it died with her, quiet and complete.
wasteland.ev.legacy.3.text: Ash has dug a fresh row of graves after the raid on the Salt Line. He holds out a chisel and asks which names go on the stones, and which men get none.
wasteland.ev.legacy.3.write.note: You cut nine names into soft stone and skinned your knuckles doing it. Ash said nothing, then planted a marker over the one nobody had claimed.
wasteland.ev.legacy.3.silent.note: The stones went up bare. Travelers will read them as a count, not a graveyard, and Ash will not ask you to help again.
wasteland.ev.legacy.4.text: The Trader keeps a scrap-archive in his truck: paper, film, a wax cylinder. He says a true story from the wastes fetches real water, and he wants yours.
wasteland.ev.legacy.4.write.note: He pressed your voice onto wax and paid in silver. Somewhere down the Caravan Companies, a stranger now knows your worst day by heart.
wasteland.ev.legacy.4.silent.note: You walked out with your jaw shut tight. The Trader logged you as a man with nothing to sell, which is its own kind of warning.
wasteland.ev.temptation.1.text: A Fixer opens his case in the Rustmarket shade: pre-Burn glitter, still sealed, enough to erase a bad week. He names a price you could almost pay.
wasteland.ev.temptation.1.resist.note: You left the case shut and your head clear. The craving did not leave; it just learned your address.
wasteland.ev.temptation.1.yield.note: Two days burned off the calendar and most of your caps with them. You woke in a drainpipe with sand in your teeth and no memory of the deal.
wasteland.ev.temptation.2.text: A caravan died of thirst on the Glass Flats, wagons still lashed. Their water drums are full, and no one is left to charge you for a drink.
wasteland.ev.temptation.2.resist.note: You counted the bodies before you counted the water. You walked on with a dry throat and a quiet conscience, and only one of those lasted.
wasteland.ev.temptation.2.yield.note: The water was warm and tasted of copper. Their canteens hung on your belt for a month before you could stand to trade them.
wasteland.ev.temptation.3.text: Mother Price turns to argue with a hauler, and the Cistern tap runs free beside you. One thimble more is the difference between a dry mouth and a wet one.
wasteland.ev.temptation.3.resist.note: You capped your bottle at the line and stepped away. Mother Price never saw, which is the only reason it counted.
wasteland.ev.temptation.3.yield.note: The extra thimble went down easy. Her ledger missed it, but the pump-hand saw everything, and he remembers faces.
wasteland.ev.temptation.4.text: A traveler sits dead against a Long Road mile-marker, picked over by vultures. His pack lies open, and something glints under the flap, still his.
wasteland.ev.temptation.4.resist.note: You put a stone over his face and kept walking. The glint stayed in your eye for a mile, then faded, then did not.
wasteland.ev.temptation.4.yield.note: It was a brass compass, worth a rifle. It has never once pointed you anywhere but back to that mile-marker.
wasteland.ev.rescue.1.text: A scavenger is pinned under a fallen girder in the Bonefield, one leg folded wrong. The rust is settling around him, and it will settle on him next.
wasteland.ev.rescue.1.help.note: You got him out with a jack and half your water. He owes you his leg, and debts like that get paid in strange coin.
wasteland.ev.rescue.1.pass.note: You heard the girder settle from a hundred paces. You did not turn around, and you know exactly what that means.
wasteland.ev.rescue.2.text: The Boy broke his shin in a scrap pit and sits in the ditch, jaw set, refusing to ask for anything. His slingshot is cocked at your knees.
wasteland.ev.rescue.2.help.note: He bit your arm while you set the bone and thanked you by stealing nothing. From the Boy, that was a treaty.
wasteland.ev.rescue.2.pass.note: You walked past a cocked slingshot. He did not fire, which was somehow worse than if he had.
wasteland.ev.rescue.3.text: The Rustborn hit the Cistern fence at dusk, and a stranger bleeds out against the gate. The guards are busy, and no one moves to drag him in.
wasteland.ev.rescue.3.help.note: You left a blood trail to your own door. The scent of it will follow you through the next two markets.
wasteland.ev.rescue.3.pass.note: You kept your hands empty and your name off the ledger. The man's boots stayed where they fell, and someone else took them.
wasteland.ev.rescue.4.text: A woman is trapped in a beached hull at Dry Harbor with the rad-wind coming in off the flats. She can hear you. She cannot climb out.
wasteland.ev.rescue.4.help.note: You tore your hands on rusted strapping and walked her out ahead of the dust. Her dosimeter clicked for both of you that night.
wasteland.ev.rescue.4.pass.note: You made shelter before the glass hit. Her voice carried a long way through the wind, and then it did not.
wasteland.ev.bargain.1.text: At Rustmarket the Trader weighs a working filter against your rifle. Clean water every day, or a gun that only matters on the worst day.
wasteland.ev.bargain.1.deal.note: You drank filtered water all season and slept worse for it. A rifle is a thing you notice missing only once.
wasteland.ev.bargain.1.walk.note: You kept your sights and your thirst. The Trader marked you as a hard sell, and hard sells pay more in the end.
wasteland.ev.bargain.2.text: Mother Price offers a week of rations if you haul buckets up the Cistern stair for six days. The stair is deep, and the buckets are heavier than they look.
wasteland.ev.bargain.2.deal.note: Your back hardened and your stomach stopped arguing. Mother Price wrote your name in her ledger, which is not always a safe place to be.
wasteland.ev.bargain.2.walk.note: You kept your hands free and your canteen light. On the fourth night, thirst made the decision for you anyway.
wasteland.ev.bargain.3.text: A Caravan driver is one gun short on the Salt Line run. He offers fuel and passage for your eyes on the horizon.
wasteland.ev.bargain.3.deal.note: You rode the whole haul with your finger off the trigger. Fuel in the tank, and one more man in the Companies who owes you a lane.
wasteland.ev.bargain.3.walk.note: You watched the convoy shrink into the dust. Three days later their wagon frames came back on a flatbed, and no one asked who was missing.
wasteland.ev.bargain.4.text: A prospector in the Bonefield wants to sell you a hand-drawn map to an untouched cache. The ink is fresh and so is the confidence.
wasteland.ev.bargain.4.deal.note: You paid for ink and walked it twice. The cache was a collapsed cellar with a dead dog in it, and the prospector was three towns gone.
wasteland.ev.bargain.4.walk.note: You left him holding his paper. He cursed you politely and sold the same map to a boy before sundown.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.1.text: The rad-wind comes off the Glass Flats while you are caught in the open. A stranger's sealed bunker stands fifty paces off, door cracked, a light showing.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.1.shelter.note: He let you in and shared his filter. You owe a stranger a night of your roof someday, and out here that is a real debt.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.1.self.note: You wrapped your face in rag and pressed to the lee of a rock. The wind sanded your voice away for a week.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.2.text: A dust storm swallows the Long Road. A caravan has circled its wagons and lit a lamp, and there is an empty slot between two wheels.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.2.shelter.note: You slept shoulder to shoulder with strangers and their dogs. Before dawn you knew every one of their names and none of their lies.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.2.self.note: You buried yourself in dust and woke half-choked. The caravan rolled on without you, and you never learned who shared that lamp.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.3.text: Rain comes down hot and stinking over the Bonefield, eating the rust. A gutted building offers one dry corner, and another survivor is already eyeing it.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.3.shelter.note: You split the corner and the silence. He told you his real name by morning, which cost him more than the roof did.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.3.self.note: You stood your ground and kept the corner to yourself. The rain ate the rest of the building, and something in you with it.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.4.text: A fall of grey ash buries Dry Harbor so thick you cannot see your hand. The Well-Keeper's half-sunk chapel glows with a single lamp.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.4.shelter.note: The masked Keeper poured you water from the chapel jug and asked no questions. You drank, and you have not forgotten the taste.
wasteland.ev.storm_night.4.self.note: You spent the night in a dead ship with your back to the steel. The ash sifted in through the seams and painted you grey.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.1.text: Cog spreads a wiring diagram across his bench and says a pump is just a promise with teeth. He offers to teach you to read it before the light goes.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.1.study.note: You traced every line until the wires made sense. The next engine you met, you did not have to trust, because you could read it.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.1.play.note: You spent the light chasing the Boy across the Cistern roofs. The diagram curled by the lamp, and Cog did not offer twice.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.2.text: The Trader chalks prices on a board and asks what a canteen is worth when the man buying is dying. He says arithmetic is the only weapon nobody can take.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.2.study.note: You learned to price a man's thirst before he knew it himself. The Trader nodded once, which was his highest praise.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.2.play.note: You gambled the evening away on knucklebones and lost your last cap. The board stayed chalked, and the lesson stayed unpriced.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.3.text: Vera lays out her bone-saw and needle and says she will teach you to close a wound before the fever sets in. The light is bad and the work is worse.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.3.study.note: You stitched a wound and did not flinch when it wept. Vera said you had the hands for it, which she never said about anyone.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.3.play.note: You spent the night at the fire drinking rotgut with scavengers. Someone else learned the stitch, and you will meet them bleeding.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.4.text: The Well-Keeper holds up a brass gauge and says a well tells the truth only to those who can read it. She offers to teach you the marks.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.4.study.note: You learned which marks meant clean and which meant the water wars were over for you. That is a harder thing to unlearn than to learn.
wasteland.ev.scholarship.4.play.note: You spent the day in Rustmarket instead of at the well head. The gauge kept its secrets, and you kept your thirst.
wasteland.ev.honor.1.text: A Caravan driver lies dying on the Long Road with a letter in his vest. He asks you to swear the road-oath and carry it to his people.
wasteland.ev.honor.1.accept.note: The oath weighed nothing and everything. You delivered the letter and gained a family you will probably have to bury.
wasteland.ev.honor.1.decline.note: You gave him water and kept your mouth shut. His people never learned his last words, and you are the only one who knows why.
wasteland.ev.honor.2.text: Mother Price summons you to stand as witness at a Cistern water trial. Testimony decides whether a family drinks this winter or walks into the wastes.
wasteland.ev.honor.2.accept.note: You said what you saw and a family stayed at the well. Mother Price now expects you honest every time she calls, which is a leash.
wasteland.ev.honor.2.decline.note: You stepped back and let another name be called. The verdict fell without you, and the family left the Cistern before dawn.
wasteland.ev.honor.3.text: A Well-Keeper offers you the old law: carry the bucket for a season and the well will remember your hands. It means walking away from everything else.
wasteland.ev.honor.3.accept.note: You hauled water until your shoulders remembered the law. The Keepers scratched a mark on your canteen that no baron has ever dared cut.
wasteland.ev.honor.3.decline.note: You handed back the rope and walked the market instead. The well forgot your face by the next ration line, the way it forgets everyone.
wasteland.ev.honor.4.text: A Rustborn raider rides in under a white rag and offers you a truce token for the camp. Taking it means speaking for a peace you cannot guarantee.
wasteland.ev.honor.4.accept.note: You took the ragged white cloth and spoke for the truce. Some in camp call you a raider's friend, and some call you the only one still alive.
wasteland.ev.honor.4.decline.note: You refused the token and cleaned your rifle that night. The truce held anyway, and you were not invited to the table that signed it.
wasteland.ev.lost.1.text: You are small and alone in the Bonefield, and Sable's voice is somewhere behind a collapsed wall. She told you to stay put, and the dogs are beginning to circle.
wasteland.ev.lost.1.call.note: Your shout carried over the rubble. She found you, and the dogs found the echo, and Sable carried you home with a bite on her calf.
wasteland.ev.lost.1.wait.note: You pressed against the wall until dark. Sable came back with a lantern and did not scold you, which frightened you more than the dogs.
wasteland.ev.lost.2.text: In the Rustmarket crowd someone shouts a name over the haggling. It might be yours, or it might be a trap wearing your boots.
wasteland.ev.lost.2.call.note: You raised your hand and the shouting stopped. The stranger studied your face and walked away, and you never learned which name he wanted.
wasteland.ev.lost.2.wait.note: You stood still until the shouting moved on. Whoever it was left Rustmarket that day without you, and the market closed over the gap.
wasteland.ev.lost.3.text: A caravan horn sounds twice through the Salt Line dust, somewhere off the road. Your ride is leaving, or a raider is calling you in.
wasteland.ev.lost.3.call.note: You whistled the old caravan signal and the horn went quiet. Whether you were heard or hunted, you never found out.
wasteland.ev.lost.3.wait.note: You crouched in the culvert until the wind passed. The caravan was three ridges gone, and the tracks told you nothing.
wasteland.ev.lost.4.text: At night on the Glass Flats a single fire burns far off, too steady for a caravan and too patient for a raider. Someone wants to be found.
wasteland.ev.lost.4.call.note: You answered the signal and waited for it to move. By dawn it was gone and the flats were empty, and you have wondered ever since who was patient enough to leave first.
wasteland.ev.lost.4.wait.note: You watched the fire all night and took no step toward it. By morning the ashes were cold, and the glass had kept no tracks.
wasteland.ev.dream.1.text: You dream of a field that is not glass or dust but grass, knee-high and moving, with rain in the air and no dosimeter clicking.
wasteland.ev.dream.1.follow.note: You stayed until the dream thinned like smoke. You woke with wet eyes and a calm that lasted most of the day.
wasteland.ev.dream.1.wake.note: You bit your tongue and woke in the dark. The field was gone, and the dust on the floor was exactly where you left it.
wasteland.ev.dream.2.text: Vera's lamp is lit and your father walks in through the door, canteen full, saying nothing, the way he did before he went out to the dry wells.
wasteland.ev.dream.2.follow.note: You crossed the room to meet him and the dream broke at your touch. You spent the morning checking the lamp was real.
wasteland.ev.dream.2.wake.note: You refused to look at him and the dream dissolved. Vera found you awake before dawn, and neither of you said the name.
wasteland.ev.dream.3.text: You dream the Cistern is full to the brim, taps running free, children drinking without a ledger. The Conclave is nowhere, and nobody is counting.
wasteland.ev.dream.3.follow.note: You drank in the dream until your chest ached. You woke with a dry mouth and the sound of running water still in your ears.
wasteland.ev.dream.3.wake.note: You pulled yourself out before your lips touched the water. The Cistern was as low as ever, and the dream stayed a debt.
wasteland.ev.dream.4.text: You dream of a house from before the Burn, with a door that shuts soft and no gun ports on the walls. Someone is cooking, and they know your name.
wasteland.ev.dream.4.follow.note: You ate a meal that never existed and woke fuller than you should have been, and lonelier than you were.
wasteland.ev.dream.4.wake.note: You opened the door and the dream fell apart like ash. You woke facing the real door, barred, exactly as you left it.
wasteland.ev.bet.1.text: In a Rustmarket back room a Fixer deals cards and the caps pile high. The man across from you is drunk and winning, and his hands are slow.
wasteland.ev.bet.1.match.note: He was slower than he was drunk. You won the pot and a reputation, and the Fixer saved you a chair at the next game, which is not a kindness.
wasteland.ev.bet.1.fold.note: You folded early and kept your stake. The drunk man lost everything and staggered out, and the table forgot you by the next deal.
wasteland.ev.bet.2.text: A Salt Line crew sets tin cans on a wagon tailgate and wagers a rifle on who shoots straighter. The wind is up and their money is down.
wasteland.ev.bet.2.match.note: You took the shot and the wind took the bullet. You paid the rifle and kept the memory of the barrel waving.
wasteland.ev.bet.2.fold.note: You left the cans standing and kept your iron. Their best man missed anyway, and the crew had no one to blame but the wind.
wasteland.ev.bet.3.text: A knife fight is fixed in the Cistern pit and half the camp is betting. The favored man is bleeding already, and the odds are ugly.
wasteland.ev.bet.3.match.note: You took the long odds on a bleeding man. He won on pure spite and split the take, then never spoke to you again.
wasteland.ev.bet.3.fold.note: You sat out the pit with your purse closed. The wounded man died of it, and the camp never forgave the men who bet against him.
wasteland.ev.bet.4.text: Two caravan hands wager on who reaches Dry Harbor first and need a third to hold the stakes. The road is bad and the night is coming.
wasteland.ev.bet.4.match.note: You held the money and watched both men ride into the dark. Only one came back, and the wager went to his widow, which nobody had written down.
wasteland.ev.bet.4.fold.note: You refused to hold the pot and walked away. One man died on that road, and the other told everyone you had taken the money when no one was looking.
wasteland.ev.hermit.1.text: At the Cistern's edge an old woman lives inside a cut-down fuel tank and reads the grit at the bottom of a canteen like scripture. She says your water is two days from turning, and will teach the trick for one mouthful.
wasteland.ev.hermit.1.learn.note: Her thumb traced the silt. By dusk you could smell bad water before it killed you.
wasteland.ev.hermit.1.mock.note: You drank the canteen dry that night and spent dawn on your knees in the dust.
wasteland.ev.hermit.2.text: A deaf old scavenger keeps watch from the tallest girder in the Bonefield, reading the horizon through the steel. Raider engines, he says, come up through your boots long before they come over the ridge.
wasteland.ev.hermit.2.learn.note: You held the cold girder and felt a convoy rolling hours before its dust showed on the sky.
wasteland.ev.hermit.2.mock.note: He never heard it. The Rustborn patrol on the ridge did.
wasteland.ev.hermit.3.text: In a beached ship at Dry Harbor a gaunt hermit scratches maps into the sand with an empty casing, claiming he charted the last clean well before the Well-Keepers cut out his tongue. He wants a full canteen for the secret.
wasteland.ev.hermit.3.learn.note: The sand pointed past the Salt Line, to water nobody had ever bothered to guard.
wasteland.ev.hermit.3.mock.note: He watched you erase it, then turned his back and never spoke again.
wasteland.ev.hermit.4.text: Out on the Glass Flats a hermit keeps a patch of weeds alive on her own ration, sure the green is coming back. She says the old woman who fed the dogs at the Cistern taught her which water they answer to.
wasteland.ev.hermit.4.learn.note: You gave a mouthful to a weed and felt, absurdly, that the ground now owed you one back.
wasteland.ev.hermit.4.mock.note: You ground the green under your boot, and the mirror sand opened your arm on the way out.
wasteland.ev.quiet.text: The wind drops and the camp goes silent, no engines, no gunfire. For one hour you hear your own pulse and nothing else.
wasteland.ev.omen.text: A cloud the color of clean water drifts over the Salt Line, and the wild dogs at the Cistern let you pass without a growl. Word travels that you are worth following.
wasteland.ev.hard.text: You haul salt up the Long Road until the strap cuts to bone and rad dust scours your throat raw. Half the day goes on your knees, coughing and swearing.
wasteland.ev.dread.text: You count your bullets twice and your birthdays once, then lie awake doing the arithmetic of which runs out first.
wasteland.ev.bounty.text: A scavenger's corpse in the Bonefield has gone unclaimed, and his pockets are still heavy. You take the caps and walk before anyone comes looking.
wasteland.ev.weariness.text: Two days of hard road settle into your joints, and the rad-sickness you swallowed on the Glass Flats starts to sing.
wasteland.beh.care.1: Picks the shrapnel out of your arm
wasteland.beh.care.1.res: Someone dug the metal out and poured on iodine.
wasteland.beh.care.2: Stitches your gash with fishing line
wasteland.beh.care.2.res: The wound closed, ugly but shut.
wasteland.beh.care.3: Cauterizes the cut with a red-hot knife
wasteland.beh.care.3.res: The bleeding stopped. The smell stayed.
wasteland.beh.meal.1: Shares a can of cold beans
wasteland.beh.meal.1.res: A can of beans, split down the middle.
wasteland.beh.meal.2: Brings you half a roasted rat
wasteland.beh.meal.2.res: You ate meat, and did not ask what kind.
wasteland.beh.meal.3: Pours you a cup of boiled rainwater
wasteland.beh.meal.3.res: The water was brown. It was water.
wasteland.beh.coin.1: Slips you a handful of bottle caps
wasteland.beh.coin.1.res: Your pockets got heavier with scrap-coin.
wasteland.beh.coin.2.res: Someone squared your tab at the Cistern.
wasteland.beh.coin.3: Drops a pouch of silver on your table
wasteland.beh.coin.3.res: A pouch of real silver, no questions.
wasteland.beh.talk.1: Complains about the rads with you
wasteland.beh.talk.1.res: Small talk about the wind and the dosimeter.
wasteland.beh.talk.2.res: You learned who is moving, and who is dead on the road.
wasteland.beh.talk.3: Sits up all night swapping war stories
wasteland.beh.talk.3.res: By dawn you were not strangers anymore.
wasteland.beh.teach.1: Shows you how to strip a wire
wasteland.beh.teach.1.res: You learned to pull copper without cooking yourself.
wasteland.beh.teach.2: Teaches you to read a dosimeter
wasteland.beh.teach.2.res: You can tell a hot zone from a bad rumor now.
wasteland.beh.teach.3: Walks you through rebuilding a pump
wasteland.beh.teach.3.res: You could fix a well with your eyes closed.
wasteland.beh.train.2: Spars in the dust until you drop
wasteland.beh.train.2.res: You learned to take a hit and stay standing.
wasteland.beh.train.3: Drags you on a dawn junk-haul
wasteland.beh.train.3.res: Your back and arms grew hard as rebar.
wasteland.beh.warn.1: Warns you the Well-Keeper is watching
wasteland.beh.warn.1.res: You kept your hands clean in front of the Keepers.
wasteland.beh.warn.2: Tips you off about a raider moon
wasteland.beh.warn.2.res: You were warned before the Rustborn rode.
wasteland.beh.warn.3: Tells you which Fixer is lying
wasteland.beh.warn.3.res: You dodged a broker's knife in the dark.
wasteland.beh.gift.1: Tosses you a live grenade, pin bent back
wasteland.beh.gift.1.res: A grenade with the pin bent back—gift and threat at once.
wasteland.beh.gift.2: Leaves you a box of pristine rounds
wasteland.beh.gift.2.res: Boxed ammunition, still sealed. Wealth on the hoof.
wasteland.beh.gift.3.res: A dosimeter, clicking faithfully. Worth its weight in water.
wasteland.beh.song.1.res: A jingle from before the Burn, half remembered.
wasteland.beh.song.2.res: The road song steadied your feet.
wasteland.beh.song.3: Sings the low ballad of the dry sea
wasteland.beh.song.3.res: The old ballad of the drowned harbor.
wasteland.beh.rest.1: Takes first watch and lets you doze
wasteland.beh.rest.1.res: You slept while someone watched the dark.
wasteland.beh.rest.2: Bars the door and kills the lamp
wasteland.beh.rest.2.res: The room went black and safe.
wasteland.beh.rest.3.res: You slept with both eyes closed—rare, out here.
wasteland.beh.debt.1.res: A clip of your ammo walked off.
wasteland.beh.debt.2: Makes you cover his water tab
wasteland.beh.debt.2.res: You paid someone's debt at the Cistern.
wasteland.beh.debt.3: Leans on you for a full drum of fuel
wasteland.beh.debt.3.res: A drum of fuel, gone and not coming back.
wasteland.beh.rumor.1.res: A whisper that your fuel is cut.
wasteland.beh.rumor.2: Tells the market you're a coward
wasteland.beh.rumor.2.res: Someone called you yellow behind your back.
wasteland.beh.rumor.3: Spreads word you killed for scrap
wasteland.beh.rumor.3.res: The rumor that you would kill a man for his boots.
wasteland.beh.taunt.1.res: A jeer about your aim, loud enough to stick.
wasteland.beh.taunt.2.res: The laugh found every scar you have earned.
wasteland.beh.taunt.3: Calls you soft, a waste of air
wasteland.beh.taunt.3.res: The insult sat in your chest all night.
wasteland.beh.scheme.1: Lifts a canister from your stash
wasteland.beh.scheme.1.res: A canister of fuel went missing.
wasteland.beh.scheme.2: Seals your well and walks away
wasteland.beh.scheme.3: Sends the Rustborn to your door
wasteland.beh.scheme.3.res: A raider patrol found your camp.
wasteland.beh.upkeep.1: Patches your roof before the rad-wind
wasteland.beh.upkeep.1.res: The roof held through the dust.
wasteland.beh.upkeep.2.res: Your scrap fetched a fair price.
wasteland.beh.upkeep.3: Watches your camp while you travel
wasteland.beh.upkeep.3.res: Your stash was waiting, untouched, when you got back.
wasteland.off.visit.1: Come to my place. Bring nothing.
wasteland.off.visit.1.text: They wave you toward a lean-to at the edge of camp, saying it's only water and quiet.
wasteland.off.visit.1.yes.res: You shared a canteen and a little silence.
wasteland.off.visit.1.no.res: They shrugged and capped the canteen.
wasteland.off.visit.2: Stay the night, the rad-wind's up.
wasteland.off.visit.2.text: They offer you floor-space behind a sealed door while the wind scrubs the camp.
wasteland.off.visit.2.yes.res: You slept safe behind a barricade.
wasteland.off.visit.2.no.res: You walked home through the grit.
wasteland.off.favor.1: Hold my stash till I'm back.
wasteland.off.favor.1.text: They ask you to guard a sack of salvage, saying it's not heavy, just theirs.
wasteland.off.favor.1.yes.res: The sack was there when they returned.
wasteland.off.favor.1.no.res: They found someone else to trust.
wasteland.off.favor.2: Say I was with you last night.
wasteland.off.favor.2.text: They need you to swear they were beside you when the Rustborn hit the camp.
wasteland.off.favor.2.yes.res: Your word bought them an alibi.
wasteland.off.venture.1: Half a tank of fuel if you drive.
wasteland.off.venture.1.text: A salvage run, split down the middle—if you've got the nerve and the fuel.
wasteland.off.venture.1.yes.res: You came back with more than you left with.
wasteland.off.venture.2: There's a cache under the Dry Harbor.
wasteland.off.venture.2.text: A rumored cache in a beached ship, if someone will front the digging.
wasteland.off.venture.2.yes.res: What you found paid for the shovel.
wasteland.off.venture.2.no.res: The cache stayed under the sand.
wasteland.off.feast.1.text: Someone's got a fire and something on it, and says there's room by the flames.
wasteland.off.feast.1.yes.res: A hot meal and warmer company.
wasteland.off.feast.2.text: A caravan crew is roasting something over a drum fire and passing the bottle around.
wasteland.off.feast.2.yes.res: You sang with strangers till the fire died.
wasteland.off.feast.2.no.res: You kept your back to the fire.
wasteland.off.secret.1: I know what's in the Cistern's vault.
wasteland.off.secret.1.text: They lean close and offer a secret about the Conclave's water stores.
wasteland.off.secret.1.yes.res: You learned where the water is really kept.
wasteland.off.secret.1.no.res: They swallowed the secret back down.
wasteland.off.secret.2: I know who cut your water line.
wasteland.off.secret.2.text: They say they know who poisoned your well—but the name has a price.
wasteland.off.secret.2.yes.res: You got a name, and a debt to pay for it.
wasteland.off.duel.1: Range contest, tin cans at fifty.
wasteland.off.duel.1.text: Someone sets up cans on a rusted girder and asks who shoots straighter.
wasteland.off.duel.1.yes.res: You out-shot them before the wind changed.
wasteland.off.duel.1.no.res: They took the win by forfeit.
wasteland.off.duel.2.text: A challenger wants it settled properly: first blood, no guns, no grudges after.
wasteland.off.duel.2.yes.res: You drew first blood and made a wary friend.
wasteland.off.duel.2.no.res: They called you afraid, and kept their edge.
wasteland.off.trade.1.text: A broker offers clean water for your rounds, a fair rate for once.
wasteland.off.trade.1.yes.res: You drank easier and shot fewer.
wasteland.off.trade.1.no.res: You kept your ammo and stayed thirsty.
wasteland.off.trade.2: A working rifle for your scrap.
wasteland.off.trade.2.text: They offer a rifle that actually fires for the pile of scrap you have been hauling.
wasteland.off.trade.2.yes.res: The rifle fired true. Your load got lighter.
wasteland.off.trade.2.no.res: You hauled the scrap home again.
wasteland.off.journey.1.text: A caravan is leaving at dawn and needs a spare pair of eyes.
wasteland.off.journey.1.yes.res: You saw new ground and came back paid.
wasteland.off.journey.2: I'm going to find the last well.
wasteland.off.journey.2.text: They mean to walk into the deep wastes and look for the well the barons never found.
wasteland.off.journey.2.no: That's a grave, not a road
wasteland.off.journey.2.yes.res: You went farther than you had ever dared.
wasteland.off.journey.2.no.res: They went alone. You kept the map.
wasteland.plugin.desc: Scrap, water, and bad blood: the small doings of survivors in a used-up world.
